summary.text: Mike Rounds is the Republican U.S. Senator from South Dakota, seeking a third term. A former insurance and real estate businessman, he served in the South Dakota Senate (1991-2000, including as majority leader) and as the state's governor (2003-2011) before his election to the Senate in 2014. He was re-elected in 2020 and won the 2026 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Rounds was born in Huron, South Dakota, the eldest of 11 children, and describes himself as a lifelong South Dakotan.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from South Dakota State University in 1977.
In the private sector he built an insurance and real estate business with offices throughout the state.
Rounds was elected five times to the South Dakota Senate and served from 1991 to 2000, as minority whip from 1993 to 1994 and as majority leader from 1995 to 2000.
He served as the state's 31st governor from 2003 to 2011.
In 2014 he won the Republican primary on June 3 and the open Senate seat in November with 50.4% of the vote, taking office in January 2015.
Rounds won re-election in 2020 with 65.7% of the vote after defeating Republican primary challenger Scyller Borglum, 75.2% to 24.8%.
According to his official biography, he serves on the Appropriations, Armed Services, Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, Indian Affairs, and Select Intelligence committees.
He won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary with 75.8% of the vote over Justin McNeal, and Ballotpedia lists President Donald Trump among his 2026 endorsers.
Rounds lives in Fort Pierre and has four grown children and 11 grandchildren, according to his official biography.
